sources.title: Yuri Bregel, Bukhara iii: After the Mongol Invasion, Encyclopaedia Iranica
sources.note: Direct original scholarly article read. Covers Shaybanid, Janid and Manghit phases, Russian domination, Islamic learning and multilingual city. Do not equate a particular modern map outline with its historical claims.

sources.title: Anke von Kügelgen, Manghits, Encyclopaedia Iranica
sources.note: Direct read. Effective dynasty from 1747, formal khan title 1756; Shah Morad 1785; nineteenth-century autonomy and Russian subordination; failed reform promises and 1920 deposition. Avoid false single foundation for the state across changing dynasties.

sources.title: Robert D. McChesney, Central Asia xi: Economy from the Timurids until the Eighteenth Century
sources.note: Indexed original text read; direct HTML failed. Sections on water, manufacturing and international trade. Mid-sixteenth-century Molla Amiri quarter occupational records; canal-based districts; 1585 diplomatic gifts. Entire work charged together, including alternate PDF extraction.

sources.title: Robert D. McChesney, Juybaris, Encyclopaedia Iranica
sources.note: Direct read. Family property and waqf documents, public institutions and employees, Ay Padshah Bibi’s 1671 madrasas and water tank. Surviving documentary evidence distinguished from standing monuments.

sources.title: ICOMOS evaluation of Historic Centre of Bukhara, World Heritage nomination 602
sources.note: Direct PDF read, English History and Description, printed pages 71 to 72. Concrete building names and 1848 counts used. Its political shorthand for 1868 incorporation is replaced with more precise protectorate language from Iranica/LoC; erroneous eleventh-century dating of Kalyan minaret not used.

sources.title: The Metropolitan Museum of Art, Cover, early nineteenth century, object 21.114.3
sources.note: Indexed original object record read. Attributed to Bukhara, silk embroidery on linen. Curatorial explanation describes typical joined cotton-strip working practice; public prose distinguishes general technique from this object’s linen ground. Family work, dowry and seams.

sources.title: Charles C. Torrey, Gold Coins of Khokand and Bukhara (ANS, 1950), catalogue no. 12
sources.note: Indexed original ANS full catalogue text read, with Arabic-script transcription at no. 12. Original PDF text also read at pahar.in/pahar/Books%20and%20Articles/Central%20Asia/1950%20Gold%20Coins%20of%20Khokand%20and%20Bukhara%20by%20Torrey%20s.pdf, printed pages 35 to 36 (human PDF 41 to 42). No. 12 is Nasr Allah, Bukhara AH 1257, gold, 4.55 grams. Mint phrase ضرب بخارا is reproduced from transcription; literal translation supplied here. Screenshot cache missed and direct PDF download denied, so no visual coin examination claimed.

sources.title: Library of Congress, Tarikh-i huzn al-milal-i Bukhara, LCCN 2002362443
sources.note: Indexed original institutional catalogue read. Last amir’s Persian memoir dated 1921, printed Paris, with map incorporating information after 1925. Catalogue dates accession 1910 and Red Army overthrow September 1920; no inference that digitized edition was wholly printed in 1921.

sources.title: Karin Rührdanz, Kolangi, Mir Hosayn Hosayni, Encyclopaedia Iranica
sources.note: Direct original scholarly article read. Named calligrapher’s work in Abd al-Aziz’s Bukhara book workshop; four Jami works, Chester Beatty Per 213, copied AH 955/1548 to 1549. Biography does not establish universal literacy.
